highlights.title: The extended mind thesis and digital knowledge systems
highlights.excerpt: If a notebook is part of the mind, then a knowledge graph with memory formation, maintenance, and gap detection is a stronger case for cognitive extension than any static tool.

highlights.title: Why retrieval is not enough
highlights.excerpt: The architectural bet of this system is that personal knowledge needs memory formation, memory maintenance, gap detection, and generative synthesis — not just search.

highlights.title: Entropy as ignorance, not disorder
highlights.excerpt: Lloyd's framing inverts the pedagogy: thermodynamics follows from information theory, not the reverse.

highlights.title: Discrete channels fail loudly, continuous channels fail silently
highlights.excerpt: The central empirical finding: wrong-answer entropy rises monotonically with noise in discrete channels but stays flat in continuous ones.

highlights.title: The gap is the product
highlights.excerpt: A recommendation system that optimises for intellectual growth treats the gap — not engagement — as the signal worth surfacing.

highlights.title: Spike-sorted anchor units as a biological sync signal
highlights.excerpt: When the hardware sync channel is flat, reward-responsive neurons that fire at a fixed latency after each event become the clock.

highlights.title: Provenance over convenience
highlights.excerpt: Every note knows its source, timestamp, confidence, and whether it is your output or external input.

highlights.title: Languages partition concept space suboptimally
highlights.excerpt: A speaker-count-weighted centroid vocabulary would lower the entry barrier for every native language while making untranslatable concepts explicit rather than silently lost.
